newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1996 current account surplus $7.242 bln.
newsitem.headline: China 1996 current account surplus $7.242 bln.

text.p: China's current account surplus in 1996 was $7.242 billion and the capital account surplus $39.967 billion, the Financial News said on Friday, quoting figures from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.

No figures were available for 1995 with officials saying earlier only that China had a balance of payments surplus of about $7.0 billion in 1995 and that this had been expected to drop sharply in 1996.

China's international balance of payments remained healthy with the current account surplus maintaining a relatively large surplus and maintaining a net inflow of capital on the capital account, the administration said.
Reserve assets continued to increase, it said.
Within the current account, it gave the trade surplus as $19.535 billion, the invisibles deficit as $14.422 billion and a surplus of $2.129 billion on unilateral transfers, it said.

Based on international standards, China's total foreign trade stood at $282.62 billion in 1996, up by 1.9 percent, it said. That was composed of exports of $151.077 billion, up by 1.6 percent from 1995 while imports were up by 4.8 percent, it said.
Income on the invisibles account, including tourism, showed a deficit, it said but gave no figures.

On the capital account, there was a significant increase in capital inflows, especially direct foreign investment. Long-term capital inflow of $69.721 billion included direct investment of $42.35 billion, which was up 12.23 percent from the previous year, it said.
Reserve assets also showed an increase by end-1996 of $31.651 billion, it said.

China's foreign exchange reserves rose by $31.431 billion by the end of 1996, while its special drawing rights rose by $32 million and its reserve position with the International Monetary Fund increased by $188 million, it said.
China posted a surplus of $7.66 billion in its international balance of payments in 1994 against a deficit of $11.9 billion in 1993.
